name: s2
diagnosis: Dominant pattern is premature FDIR consumption: a mild friction fault around 0.2 severity with residual around 0.46 mNm trips first and consumes the single isolation slot. Later severe friction or derate cannot be isolated, leaving 3-wheel control including the worst wheel. With no isolation 4-wheel pseudo-inverse stays controllable, so violation is policy-induced.
rule_in_words: Only isolate a wheel that trips the detector if its residual is at least 0.5 mNm; milder tripping wheels are only flagged and remain in control.
rationale: Threshold sits just above observed mild-friction trip residuals 0.455-0.49 mNm and below hard derate and severe residuals 0.52-0.65 mNm. It suppresses the wrong first isolation, keeps 4-wheel control through mild faults, and leaves the single slot free for a later hard fault. That restores control on the three healthiest wheels and addresses both attitude-loss and saturation double-fault patterns without swaps or re-admits.
why_no_regressions: Change only removes isolations, never adds isolation, swap, SAFE entry or resume change. Runs with no isolation are bit-identical. Runs with hard failures still exceed 0.5 mNm and still isolate, only slightly deferred. Mild-only runs stay on 4 wheels which no-policy traces show controllable.
ideal_rule_if_unconstrained: Rank wheels by continuous health estimate and always control on healthiest three, allowing swap to worse fault and second isolation to under-actuated mode with ground override.
gate_reason: rejected (strict): 3 new violations in 3 runs (3 previously clean), 3 fixes, 794 runs evaluated (stopped early)
